before.question:
**Matrix Multiplication.** Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$.

Compute the product $AB$ by finding each entry as a row-by-column dot product. Give the complete resulting $2 \times 2$ matrix.

solution_steps.title: Understand the Setup
solution_steps.description:
Matrix multiplication works by pairing each **row of $A$** with each **column of $B$** and taking a dot product — meaning we multiply matching entries and add the results.

For two $2 \times 2$ matrices, the result $AB$ is also a $2 \times 2$ matrix where entry $(i, j)$ = (row $i$ of $A$) $\cdot$ (column $j$ of $B$).

There are exactly **4 entries** to compute, one for each $(i,j)$ combination: $(1,1),\ (1,2),\ (2,1),\ (2,2)$.

solution_steps.title: Assemble the Result
solution_steps.description:
Place the four computed entries into their correct positions:
$$AB = \begin{pmatrix} (1,1) & (1,2) \\ (2,1) & (2,2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 36 \\ 3 & 30 \end{pmatrix}$$

ai_reply_text: I've made the product undefined by changing B to a 3×2 matrix — a 2×2 matrix can't be multiplied by a 3×2 matrix since the inner dimensions don't match (2 ≠ 3). The solution now explains why the product is undefined.

after.question:
**Matrix Multiplication.** Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$.

Can the product $AB$ be computed? Explain why or why not by checking the dimensions of each matrix.
after.final_answer: The product $AB$ is **undefined** because $A$ is $2 \times 2$ and $B$ is $3 \times 2$; the inner dimensions $2 \neq 3$ so the matrices are not conformable for multiplication.

solution_steps.title: Identify the Dimensions
solution_steps.description:
First, state the size of each matrix.

- Matrix $A$ has **2 rows and 2 columns** → it is a $2 \times 2$ matrix.
- Matrix $B$ has **3 rows and 2 columns** → it is a $3 \times 2$ matrix.

solution_steps.title: Check the Conformability Rule
solution_steps.description:
For a product $AB$ to exist, the **number of columns in $A$** must equal the **number of rows in $B$**.

$$\underbrace{A}_{2 \times \mathbf{2}} \times \underbrace{B}_{\mathbf{3} \times 2}$$

The inner dimensions are **2 and 3**. Since $2 \neq 3$, the matrices are **not conformable** for multiplication.

solution_steps.title: State the Conclusion
solution_steps.description: Because the number of columns of $A$ (which is 2) does **not** equal the number of rows of $B$ (which is 3), the product $AB$ is **undefined**.
